The `HelpFormatter.printHelp` method is responsible for printing the help for options with the specified command line syntax. It takes parameters including the writer to which the help will be written, the width of characters to be displayed on each line, the command line syntax, the header and footer banners, the options instance, the padding for each line, and the padding for description lines.

The failing test `testLongLineChunkingIndentIgnored` sets up an `Options` instance with a long description, creates a `HelpFormatter`, and then prints the help with a width of 22 characters. The expected output contains the description split into multiple lines to fit the width.

The current bug report describes an issue where `HelpFormatter` goes into an infinite loop if there is not enough space to display a word on a single line, leading to a JVM crash with an OutOfMemoryError.

To diagnose this issue, we need to investigate the logic within the `HelpFormatter.printHelp` method to understand how it handles long descriptions and line wrapping.

Next, I will inspect the relevant code snippet of the `HelpFormatter.printHelp` method to identify any potential issues leading to the infinite loop.

To address the issue described in the bug report of an infinite loop causing a JVM crash with an OutOfMemoryError, the recursive call within the `printHelp` method needs to have a proper termination condition to prevent it from going into an infinite loop.
